source.title: Hybrid method of conventional neural network training

record.file_problem: None; the full text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training outcomes for convolutional networks on Iris and MNIST, extending the training-convergence question to datasets outside the claim versions’ stated settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own training results on Iris and MNIST. Its military-image accuracy result is stated without a training-error value or recipe details, so it is not recorded as a row. Cited findings are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study uses He et al. (2015) initialization (Section 4) and compares its hybrid optimizer with Adam and Levenberg–Marquardt on Iris and MNIST. These results measure optimizer performance, without testing any version's specified training-error, width, depth, initialization, stability-threshold, or normalization effect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report better convergence than Adam, training where Adam exhibits paralysis, and error within 10 dB of Levenberg–Marquardt. They also emphasize adjustable computational complexity and mini-batch compatibility. Their stated applicability conditions are limited training time and sufficient resources for Hessian-related computations. Their broad claim of fewer operations than Adam should be qualified: Table 2 gives higher hybrid cost per epoch, while the MNIST comparison concerns equivalent total computation time.
record.recipe_differences: Combines Levenberg–Marquardt for classifier layers with Adam for the convolutional parameterizer; experiments use Iris and MNIST rather than the claim versions’ stated settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper says computational complexity can be adjusted by changing how many layers use Levenberg–Marquardt. It reports mini-batch training for MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: On Iris, Adam's reported training error plateaued at −23 dB; the hybrid method reportedly converged faster and remained within 10 dB of Levenberg–Marquardt.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The hybrid optimizer improves convergence over Adam on the tested small Iris network.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, 20 hybrid epochs reached −8 dB and reported 95% classification accuracy, while Adam failed to train during an equivalent computation budget of 4000 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The hybrid optimizer can train the tested MNIST network under a computation budget where Adam exhibits learning paralysis.

record.problems: Experiments cover Iris and MNIST rather than CIFAR benchmarks. The paper gives no uncertainty estimates or controls. Iris comparison values are plotted rather than stated numerically. The MNIST result reports 95% accuracy but does not give training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: The military-technology image classification accuracy of 93.5% is mentioned without a named dataset, architecture, training-error value, or comparable recipe; omitted as insufficiently specified for a row.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 networks, including corrupted labels, and dependence on size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.

Effects of initialization choice on training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth. He initialization is used without comparison; the abstract's initialization-stability statement is not backed by a reported initialization sweep.
Recovery, curvature changes, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence relative to a measured learning-rate stability threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: No version-level verdict is warranted. Adam's failure on these small networks does not challenge V1's claim about sufficiently large CIFAR networks. All three rows concern an optimizer comparison outside the versions in play.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 experiments, corrupted or random labels, model-size comparison, or stated random-initialization comparison.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or neuron-width sweep.
No depth comparison, identity-shortcut comparison, or experiments on the cited plain or residual architectures.
No comparison of activation-matched, orthogonal, or Gaussian initializations, or trainable-depth sweep.
No learning-rate-above-stability experiment, curvature or sharpness measurement, or divergence sweep.
No batch-normalization comparison or normalization-speed and learning-rate-tolerance measurement.

rows.subject: ИНС (Adam)
rows.size_stated: 4 convolutional kernels 2 × 2; 4 neurons in first hidden layer; 3 output neurons
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam on the Iris dataset; the plot shows 100 epochs.
rows.value: did not improve the error below −23 dB
rows.note: The stated result is a lower bound on improvement; no exact final error is given.
rows.check: The −23 dB plateau is correctly reported, but this normalized squared-error measure on a small Iris network cannot establish any version's effect. Replace the partial state. The text says only 100 epochs are displayed; it does not establish that training stopped at 100 epochs.

rows.subject: ИНС (гибридный алгоритм)
rows.size_stated: 4 convolutional kernels 2 × 2; 4 neurons in first hidden layer; 3 output neurons
rows.operation_detail: Trained with the proposed Levenberg–Marquardt/Adam hybrid method on Iris.
rows.baseline: Adam: did not improve below −23 dB
rows.note: The text says the hybrid converges better and faster than Adam, but the plotted value is not transcribed numerically.
rows.check: This is the proposed method's performance comparison, not evidence for a claim version. The supplied figure text does not provide a readable numerical hybrid endpoint; the prose reports better convergence than Adam and an error within 10 dB of Levenberg–Marquardt.

rows.subject: ИНС (гибридный алгоритм)
rows.size_stated: 4 convolutional kernels 3 × 3 in first convolutional layer; 5 kernels 3 × 3 in second; 12 and 11 neurons in hidden layers; 10 output neurons
rows.operation_detail: Trained in mini-batches with the proposed hybrid method on MNIST.

conditions.value: Equivalent computation time to 4000 Adam epochs

rows.baseline: Adam: network did not train at equivalent computation time
rows.value: Training error reached the −8 dB stopping criterion; classification accuracy 95%
rows.note: The text reports the hybrid outcome and equivalent-time comparison; it does not state a zero training classification error.
rows.check: The −8 dB criterion, 95% accuracy, and equivalent-time comparison are reported correctly, but measure the proposed optimizer's performance rather than a version's effect. Replace the partial state. Split squared training error and classification accuracy into separate measures if retained; the accuracy's evaluation split is unspecified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
